sources_considered.why: Primary study with performance comparisons across natural-language understanding tasks.
Establishes that the supporting study was publicly submitted in March 2022.
Contemporaneous primary counterevidence showing that pragmatic context changes the assessment.
Read the methods and conclusions to assess the scope of the counterevidence and confirm conference dates.
The October 2022 benchmark does not establish when its experiments occurred relative to the July target period.
The later evaluation includes a different model population and does not directly establish July 2022 performance.

evidence_items.locator: Table 4 caption; section 3, research question Q3
evidence_items.explanation: The study reports substantial RoBERTa performance losses on subsets where negation matters: QNLI macro F1 is 0.67 for important negations versus 0.92 for unimportant negations. These are dataset-subset comparisons, not matched sentence pairs; the findings were already reported in the March preprint.

The authors report a substantially more optimistic assessment from pragmatic tests of transformer models. This is material counterevidence to a universal inability claim, but does not establish reliable performance across the tasks implicated by e1.

unresolved_gaps: The cited evidence does not measure every contemporary architecture or establish a single population-wide negation penalty.
The supporting study's important-negation subsets are not otherwise identical to its comparison subsets.
